chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Yahya ibn Uqayl, from Hasan, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon, so he praised Allah and extolled Him.

And he said: As for what follows, indeed those who were before you were destroyed because of whatever acts of disobedience they committed, and the Rabbis and the Scholars did not forbid them from that. And when they persisted in the acts of disobedience and the Rabbis and the Scholars did not forbid them from that, the punishments descended upon them.
So enjoin the good and forbid the evil, and know that enjoining the good and forbidding the evil does not bring the term (of life) nearer nor cut off the livelihood.
Indeed, the Command descends from the sky to the earth like drops of rain to every soul, with whatever Allah has measured for it, of increase or decrease.
So if a misfortune befalls one of you in family, or wealth, or self, and he sees in his brother an abundance of family, or wealth, or self, let it not be a trial/distress for him.
For indeed the Muslim man is free from treachery as long as he does not conceal a lowliness that becomes apparent.

So he fears it when it is mentioned, and the base people are tempted by it. He is like the left-paralyzed one who awaits the first success from his dice, so that the booty is obligated for him and the debt is repelled from him.

And similarly, the Muslim man who is free from treachery awaits from Allah the Exalted one of the two good things: either the caller of Allah (death), for what is with Allah is better for him, or the sustenance of Allah.

So when he is with family and wealth, and with him is his religion and his lineage, indeed wealth and sons are the crop of the world, and righteous deeds are the crop of the Hereafter, and Allah may gather both of these for some people.

So fear Allah as He has warned you from Himself, and fear Him with a fear that is not an excuse, and work without showing off nor being heard (fame), for whoever acts for other than Allah, Allah leaves him to the one he has acted for.
We ask Allah for the stations of the martyrs, and the companionship of the happy ones, and the association of the prophets.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of enjoining good and forbidding evil in Shia tradition according to Imam Ali's sermon?
ai.summary: In this sermon from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (AS) links the divine punishment of past nations to the negligence of their *Rabbaniyyun* (scholars) in enforcing *Amr bil-Ma'ruf*, establishing it as a communal obligation rather than a mere personal virtue. He further clarifies that this practice does not curtail lifespan or sustenance, using the metaphor of rain to illustrate that divine decree remains constant regardless of human action, while warning against the spiritual danger of envy (*fitna*) which leads to treachery.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Hamza, from Yahya Bin Uqeyl, from Hasan who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> addressed, so he<sup>asws</sup> Praised Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Extolled Him<sup>azwj</sup>,

and said: ‘After this, so he rather they were destroyed, the ones who was before you where whatever they did from the acts of disobedience and their Rabbis and the Monks did not forbid them from that. And whenever they deliberated in their acts of disobedience and their Rabbis and the Monks did not forbid them from that, the Punishments descended unto them.

Therefore, enjoin with the good and forbid from the evil, and know that the enjoining of the good and the forbidding from the evil does not bring the term (death) any nearer and does not cut off the livelihood.
The Command descends from the sky to the earth like drops of the rain to every soul with whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Measured for it, from an increase or a decrease.

So, if one of your were to be hit by a difficulty in a family, or wealth, or self, and sees in the presence of his brother abundance of family, or wealth, or self, so a tribulation (distress) should not occur upon him,
for the Muslim person is away from the treachery so long he does not let his lowliness to become apparent.

So he should fear it when it is mentioned, and be tempted by it like the generality of the people, like the one paralysed on the left who is awaiting the first success from his sitting back so that the war booty would be Obligated upon him, and the fines would be repulsed from him (too long) .

And similar to that is the Muslim person who is free from the treachery, awaiting from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted, one of the two good deeds, either he supplicates to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for whatever is better for him in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, or Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Grants him sustenance.

So when he is with a family, and wealth, and with him is his religion, and it is sufficient for him that the wealth and the sons are a plantation of the world, and the righteous deeds are a plantation of the Hereafter, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Gathered both of these for a people.

Therefore, be cautious from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> has Cautioned from Himself<sup>azwj</sup>, and fear Him<sup>azwj</sup> with a fear which is not with a pretext, and work without showing off nor to be heard (become famous), for the one who acts for other than Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, He<sup>azwj</sup> Allocates him to the one who he has acted for.
We<sup>asws</sup> hereby ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for the status of the martyrs, and the happy living, and friendship of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Najran from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from abu Hamzah from Yahya ibn ‘Aqil from Hassan who has said the following:
“Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once delivered a sermon. He first praised and glorified Allah.

Thereafter he said, ‘People before were destroyed because when they committed sins the Rabbis and Monks did not stop them from committing such deeds. When they continued committing disobedience and the Rabbis and Monks did not prohibit them, torments descended upon them.
They then commanded others to do good and prohibited to commit evil, they found this did not make the time of their death closer and nor did it reduce their sustenance.
The command comes from the sky to the earth, like the drops of rain, to everyone as Allah measures for it (soul) in matters of increase and reduction.
If one of you is affected in matters of family, property or life and finds all such things with his brother in abundance, it should not become matters of trial for him.
A Muslim is free of all forms of treachery as long as acts of lowliness do not take place from him (through his hands), about the mention of which he remains fearful.
On the other hand, people of lowly manners remain interested in lowly acts like a gambler who waits for the hit by the first winning arrow which brings him gains and fends off from him the loss.

The Muslim who is free of treachery expects from Allah, the most High, one of the two forms of gains. It is either the call from Allah, thus what is with Allah for him is better, or sustenance from Allah.

So he has a family, property with religion and valuable status. Wealth and children are worldly plantations but good deeds are plantations for the next life. At certain times Allah places both of them together for certain people.

You must remain anxious about your relationship with Allah just as He has told you to be anxious about such relationship. You must worry, without shortcomings and about your status before Him. You must act without showing off and seeking popularity; those who act for something other than Allah, He leaves him to the one for whom he has acted.
I pray to Allah to lead us to the destinations of the martyrs, living of those who have gained salvation and the company of the prophets (of Allah).”’
